proposition.claim: The United States or Israel carries out a military strike against a target inside Iran within 1 day after the Strait of Hormuz reopens to substantial commercial shipping traffic.

resolution.criteria: At least one air, missile, or naval strike carried out by United States or Israeli forces against a target located in Iranian territory, Iranian territorial waters, or an Iranian-flagged vessel, occurring within 24 hours of the confirmed reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to substantial commercial shipping traffic, as confirmed by an official U.S. Department of Defense or Israel Defense Forces statement, or by Reuters or Associated Press reporting attributed to named U.S. or Israeli officials.
resolution.source: Reuters, corroborated by U.S. Department of Defense or Israel Defense Forces statements

base_rate.reference_class: Ceasefires or truce arrangements announced during the Israel/US-Iran conflict complex since June 2025 (Twelve-Day War ceasefire of 24 June 2025; 2026 Iran war ceasefire of 8 April 2026), counted where a strike by Israeli or U.S. forces against Iran or an allied front occurred within 24 hours of the ceasefire taking effect

links.rationale: A US or Israeli strike on Iran so soon after the strait reopens gives Tehran an immediate pretext and motive to retaliate against shipping or mine/patrol the strait again, which is exactly the kind of renewed attack or hostilities that would break the 30-day clean-hold requirement. Iran's own naval and IRGC forces have repeatedly used harassment of tankers as a proportionate response to strikes on its territory, so the risk of a fresh disruption jumps immediately once such a strike occurs rather than building gradually.

A US or Israeli strike on Iran the day after the Strait reopens signals that the underlying conflict is not over, reviving fears of an Iranian response against shipping or oil infrastructure. That shock would push Brent back up rather than let it settle 10% below the pre-reopening close, so the strike works directly against this claim coming true even though its main channel is through the 30-day-hold claim.

A US or Israeli strike on Iran so soon after the strait reopens raises the immediate prospect of Iranian retaliation, mining, or renewed harassment of tankers, so war-risk underwriters reprice hull cover upward within hours regardless of whether physical transits keep flowing. This is exactly the pattern seen repeatedly during the 2026 crisis, where premiums jumped from a pre-crisis baseline near 0.25% of hull value to as high as 3-10% each time fighting escalated, then eased only as calm persisted.

sources.title: Shipping insurance surges again as attacks intensify over Strait of Hormuz | The National

proposition.claim: The Strait of Hormuz reopens to substantial commercial shipping traffic within the next week.

resolution.criteria: IMF PortWatch's published daily transit count for the Strait of Hormuz reaches at least 50 commercial vessels on any single day between 21 September 2026 and 28 September 2026 (versus a pre-crisis baseline of roughly 85 transits per day and a most-recent recorded count of 8 on 13 September 2026), OR Iran's government publicly rescinds its closure declaration and transit volume visibly resumes on AIS tracking over that window.

base_rate.reference_class: Calendar weeks since the Strait of Hormuz closure began on 28 February 2026 through 21 September 2026, counting a week as 'open' if commercial transit volume broadly returned toward pre-crisis levels (the strait was not under an active closure declaration and shipping resumed) for that week \u2014 this happened only during the roughly two-week window after the 17 June 2026 Islamabad Memorandum before it collapsed in early July.

proposition.claim: The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to substantial commercial shipping traffic holds for at least 30 consecutive days, with no renewed attack, naval blockade, or hostilities forcing shipping to stop again.

resolution.criteria: Vessel-tracking data (such as Kpler or Windward AI transit counts) shows daily tanker and cargo transits through the Strait of Hormuz at or above 80% of the pre-war (2025) daily average for at least 30 consecutive days, with no interruption of transits caused by an attack, naval blockade, or renewed hostilities during that window.
resolution.source: Kpler vessel-tracking data (as reported via Reuters, Bloomberg, or Kpler's own publications)

base_rate.reference_class: Announced reopenings/ceasefires during the 2026 Iran war that were supposed to restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz (the 8 April 2026 US-Iran ceasefire and the mid-June 2026 sixty-day ceasefire), counted as a success if commercial transit volumes stayed at or above 80% of pre-war levels for 30 uninterrupted days

links.rationale: A reopening this week is the necessary starting point for any sustained 30-day period of normal traffic to even be possible; without it the clock never starts. But the 2026 war has already produced two prior reopenings/ceasefires that both broke down within weeks under renewed attacks, so the same underlying instability that could undo this one is already pushing the other way once the trigger fires.

proposition.claim: ICE Brent crude oil front-month futures settle at least 10% below their pre-reopening closing price within 5 trading days of the Strait of Hormuz reopening to substantial commercial shipping traffic.

resolution.criteria: The ICE Brent front-month futures contract's daily settlement price falls to a level at least 10% below its settlement price on the last trading day before the Strait of Hormuz reopening, at any point within 5 trading days after the reopening.
resolution.source: ICE Futures Europe daily settlement prices

base_rate.reference_class: Ceasefire or Strait-of-Hormuz-reopening announcements during the 2026 Iran-Israel-US conflict, counted from contemporaneous market reports, where Brent crude fell by at least 10% within the following week of the announcement

payoff.instrument: ICE Brent Crude Oil front-month futures

links.rationale: The Strait carries roughly a fifth of global oil supply, so a confirmed reopening to substantial traffic immediately removes the war-risk supply premium markets had built in, prompting traders to mark crude sharply lower; this pattern repeated across the 2026 conflict whenever ceasefire or reopening news broke.

proposition.claim: Average quoted war-risk insurance premiums for oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz fall back to within 0.35 percentage points of the pre-crisis baseline of 0.25% of hull replacement value.

resolution.criteria: Lloyd's List Intelligence, or an equivalent London-market shipping-insurance rate disclosure tied to the Joint War Committee's Listed Area for the Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf, reports the average quoted war-risk premium for vessels transiting that Listed Area at or below 0.60% of hull replacement value, sustained for at least one full week.
resolution.source: Lloyd's List Intelligence / London Market Joint War Committee (JWC) rate disclosures

links.rationale: Thirty consecutive days without a renewed attack, blockade or hostilities is the kind of durable, verifiable calm that underwriters and the Joint War Committee use to reassess a Listed Area; once that threshold is met, insurers begin stepping down the added war-risk premium they imposed when the JWC expanded the Gulf war zone during the crisis.

proposition.claim: US retail gasoline prices, as measured by AAA's National Average Fuel Gauge Report, fall by at least $0.15 per gallon within 21 days of the Strait of Hormuz reopening to substantial commercial shipping traffic.

resolution.criteria: AAA's National Average Fuel Gauge Report shows the US retail regular gasoline price at least $0.15 per gallon below its level on the day the Strait of Hormuz reopens to substantial commercial shipping traffic, with that drop recorded within 21 calendar days of the reopening.

links.rationale: Wholesale gasoline prices track crude oil fairly quickly, but retail pump prices are well documented to fall more slowly than they rise (the 'rockets and feathers' pattern), so a reopening that lets crude sell off still takes one to a few weeks to show up fully at the pump as refiners, wholesalers and retailers work through existing inventory and margins. Once the strait reopens and crude eases, this pass-through happens regardless of whether the strait later shuts again, since it reflects oil already purchased and shipped at the lower price.

proposition.claim: Baltic Exchange spot freight rate assessments for VLCCs on the Middle East Gulf to China route (TD3C) fall to within 30% of their January-May 2026 pre-crisis average.

resolution.criteria: The Baltic Exchange's published TD3C VLCC spot freight rate assessment (Middle East Gulf to China, US dollars per day) averages no more than 30% above the average level of that same assessment recorded between 1 January and 31 May 2026, sustained for at least 5 consecutive publishing days.

links.rationale: Once thirty days pass with no renewed attack, blockade, or hostilities, shipowners regain confidence to bid for Gulf cargoes again, the fleet that had diverted around the Cape of Good Hope returns to the shorter Hormuz route, and the risk surcharges owners had built into voyage quotes unwind, pulling spot charter rates back down from crisis peaks. Reporting during the crisis shows VLCC rates on Gulf routes spiking to multiples of normal levels (one index reaching roughly $509,000 per day, versus a typical range far below that), which is the elevated baseline this claim expects to unwind once the reopening proves durable.

resolution.criteria: NYSE closing price for Frontline plc (ticker FRO) on any trading day on or before 31 December 2026 is at least 10% below the highest closing price it recorded between 1 June 2026 and 21 September 2026.

links.rationale: War-risk insurance premiums are a direct input into VLCC voyage economics through Hormuz; while elevated they inflated freight rates and produced windfall spot earnings for owners, one report calling Frontline 'the most direct equity expression of the tanker-rate shock'. Once premiums fall back to baseline, that windfall disappears and the crisis premium built into the stock unwinds, and this repricing only persists for as long as premiums (and the de-escalation they signal) stay near baseline everse it. proposition.claim: Asian spot LNG prices, as measured by the Japan-Korea Marker benchmark, fall back to within $3.00 per MMBtu of their pre-crisis level.

resolution.criteria: The S&P Global Commodity Insights Platts Japan-Korea Marker (JKM) front-month LNG spot price assessment closes at or below $13.70 per MMBtu \u2014 within $3.00 of the pre-war level of roughly $10.70 per MMBtu recorded in late February 2026 \u2014 on at least one publication day within 60 days of the Strait of Hormuz reopening being confirmed to have held for 30 consecutive days.
resolution.source: S&P Global Commodity Insights, Platts JKM daily price assessment

links.rationale: QatarEnergy's force majeure on Ras Laffan LNG loadings, triggered by the Hormuz crisis, removed close to a fifth of global LNG supply and drove JKM up from about $10.70/MMBtu pre-war to the mid-$20s. A Hormuz reopening that stays stable for 30 days lets Qatar resume full LNG train output and steady tanker transits, easing the supply shortfall that had been propping up JKM; because that relief depends on continuous safe transit, any renewed blockade or attack would choke it off again.

sources.title: LNG market disruption: QatarEnergy extends force majeure with Edison

links.rationale: War-risk premiums are a direct, quoted line-item in the voyage cost that owners and brokers bake into Worldscale/spot freight assessments for the Gulf-to-China route; when quoted premiums fall back toward the 0.25% baseline, that cost saving is passed straight through into the freight quotes owners are willing to accept, pulling TD3C back toward its pre-crisis average within days. Because this is a live cost pass-through rather than a one-off shock, the pull only holds while premiums stay low \u2014 if war-risk rates spiked again, freight quotes would follow them back up regardless of this claim having once resolved true.

proposition.claim: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics' seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index energy index falls month-over-month in its report covering October 2026.

resolution.criteria: The seasonally adjusted CPI energy index (all urban consumers) reported for October 2026 is lower than the seasonally adjusted September 2026 level, as stated in the BLS CPI News Release covering October 2026 data.
resolution.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI News Release)

base_rate.reference_class: Seasonally adjusted month-over-month changes in the U.S. CPI energy index, March through August 2026 (6 monthly BLS releases)

links.rationale: Gasoline is the largest single component of the CPI energy index, so a nationwide $0.15/gal (roughly 4-5%) retail price decline mechanically pulls down the average gasoline price used in that month's index calculation. Once the price fall is realized within the 21-day window, it is essentially locked into that month's average and shows up as a step change in the reported energy index rather than something that fades or needs to rebuild.

proposition.claim: The U.S. Global Jets exchange-traded fund (NYSEARCA: JETS) closes at least 8% above its pre-reopening closing price at some point within 30 days of the Strait of Hormuz reopening to substantial commercial shipping traffic.

resolution.criteria: On at least one trading day within 30 calendar days after the Strait of Hormuz reopens to substantial commercial shipping traffic, the U.S. Global Jets ETF (NYSEARCA: JETS) records a closing price at least 8% higher than its closing price on the last trading day before that reopening date.
resolution.source: NYSE Arca consolidated closing price data for NYSEARCA: JETS

links.rationale: Jet fuel typically runs 20-40% of airline operating costs (IATA put the global share at 31.4% in its 2026 outlook), so a confirmed, sustained drop in pump gasoline prices signals lower crude/refined-product costs and directly lifts airline margin expectations. This exact mechanism already played out in this crisis: JETS fell from above $31 to below $24 as jet fuel prices spiked with the Hormuz war's onset, then climbed back above $33 once oil eased, and separately jumped on a later de-escalation. Markets take a few days to revise airline earnings estimates once the price decline is confirmed, then hold the repricing as long as costs stay down.

links.rationale: VLCC time-charter-equivalent earnings, and hence Frontline's revenue and stock valuation, are driven almost mechanically by the same Middle East Gulf-to-China spot rates the TD3C assessment tracks; Frontline's own Q2 2026 disclosures show VLCC spot bookings priced directly off benchmark route rates near $150,000-plus per day during the crisis spike. Once TD3C reverts to within 30% of its pre-crisis average, Frontline's forward booking rates and thus its earnings outlook fall correspondingly, which markets price into the shares within a few trading days and which persists only as long as freight rates stay depressed.

proposition.claim: The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSEARCA: XLY) closes at least 5% above its pre-reopening closing price at some point within 30 days of the Strait of Hormuz reopening to substantial commercial shipping traffic.

resolution.criteria: XLY's daily closing price, as reported on its official NYSE Arca listing, reaches a level at least 5% above the closing price recorded on the last trading day before the Strait of Hormuz reopening, at any point within the 30 calendar days following that reopening.
resolution.source: NYSE Arca closing price data for NYSEARCA: XLY

links.rationale: A sustained drop of at least $0.15/gallon frees up household cash that historically gets redirected toward discretionary categories rather than saved outright; JPMorgan Chase Institute research on the 2014-15 gas price decline found households shifted freed-up fuel savings into other spending, and 2026 retail-sales reporting has already shown discretionary categories like food services, electronics and sports goods leading gains even amid volatile gas prices. That reallocation shows up in retail sales and earnings guidance with a lag as consumers realize and then spend the savings, which is why equity investors bid up consumer-discretionary names like XLY over the following weeks rather than instantly.

proposition.claim: The front-month ICE TD3C (Baltic Exchange Middle East Gulf to China) VLCC freight future settles at least 20% below the highest front-month settlement price it recorded during the 2026 Hormuz crisis period, at some point before 31 December 2026.

resolution.criteria: The daily settlement price of the front-month ICE TD3C FFA (Middle East Gulf to China Baltic VLCC freight future) contract falls to a level at least 20% below the highest front-month settlement price recorded for that contract at any time from the onset of the 2026 Hormuz crisis through the Strait's reopening, with this threshold reached on any single trading day up to and including 31 December 2026.
resolution.source: ICE Futures (Intercontinental Exchange) daily settlement prices for the TD3C FFA Middle East Gulf to China (Baltic) Future

payoff.instrument: ICE TD3C FFA Middle East Gulf to China (Baltic) Future, front-month contract

links.rationale: TD3C freight futures are cash-settled directly against the Baltic Exchange's own TD3C spot assessment, and academic work on tanker freight markets finds spot and forward-freight prices show strong, persistent bilateral correlation. Once the spot assessment itself normalizes toward its pre-crisis average, the front-month future, which prices in near-term expectations of that same settlement index, reprices almost immediately to a comparable discount, so the two events are nearly mechanically linked rather than independent.

proposition.claim: ICE Endex Dutch TTF front-month natural gas futures settle within 15% of their January-May 2026 average closing price, at any point within 15 trading days of the Japan-Korea Marker benchmark falling back to within $3.00 per MMBtu of its pre-crisis level.

resolution.criteria: The ICE Endex Dutch TTF front-month natural gas futures contract records a daily settlement price within 15% (above or below) of the January-May 2026 average front-month settlement price, on at least one trading day within 15 trading days after the Japan-Korea Marker benchmark first falls back to within $3.00/MMBtu of its pre-crisis level, as reported in ICE Endex settlement data.

payoff.instrument: ICE Endex Dutch TTF front-month natural gas futures

links.rationale: JKM and TTF are linked by flexible-cargo arbitrage: when Qatari and other Gulf cargoes that transit Hormuz become available again and JKM eases, traders redirect fewer diverted volumes toward Asia, freeing supply back into the Atlantic basin and pulling TTF down with it. This spread-arbitrage relationship is well documented and reacts within one to two weeks of a shift in relative benchmark levels.

proposition.claim: Flex LNG Ltd (NYSE: FLNG) shares close at least 10% below the highest closing price they recorded during the 2026 Hormuz crisis period, at any point before 31 December 2026.

resolution.criteria: FLNG's daily closing share price falls, on at least one trading day up to and including 31 December 2026, to a level at least 10% below the highest closing price FLNG recorded at any point during the 2026 Hormuz crisis period (the interval from the first confirmed disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping until the Strait's reopening to substantial commercial traffic).
resolution.source: New York Stock Exchange closing price data

links.rationale: Qatar and the UAE ship the overwhelming majority of their LNG through Hormuz, and the crisis drove spot LNG charter rates up several hundred percent, lifting LNG carrier owners like Flex LNG well above pre-crisis valuations; once the Japan-Korea Marker settles back near its pre-crisis level it signals that the Qatari supply squeeze and the spot-market scramble for tonnage have unwound, so the elevated spot earnings and dividend expectations priced into FLNG fade and the market re-rates the shares down toward normalized fundamentals. Because this valuation gap tracks the ongoing spot-rate/JKM signal rather than a one-off shock, the push should persist only while JKM stays near pre-crisis levels: LNG shipping-sector indices have already been observed falling specifically on news of easing Hormuz tensions and softer gas prices.

resolution.criteria: ICE's published daily settlement price for the front-month JKM LNG (Platts) future falls to a level at least 20% below the highest front-month settlement price recorded for that contract between the onset of the 2026 Hormuz crisis and the Strait's reopening, on any settlement date up to and including 31 December 2026.

base_rate.reference_class: Major Asian JKM spot-price crisis spikes since 2020 that were followed by a decline of at least 20% from their peak within the same or the following calendar year, counting the 2022 Russia-Ukraine invasion spike as one case
